chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a newborn born on the night of Al-Fitr (Eid al-Fitr); is Zakat al-Fitr due upon it? He said, 'No, because it has exited the month.'

key_terms.خَرَجَ عَنِ الشَّهْرِ: Exited the month (referring to the conclusion of Ramadan)
key_terms.فِطْرَةٌ: Zakat al-Fitr, the obligatory charity given at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ الْفِطْرِ: The night of Eid al-Fitr (the night following the last day of Ramadan)

ai.seo_question: Is Zakat al-Fitr required for a baby born on the night of Eid al-Fitr?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq) to clarify that Zakat al-Fitr is contingent upon being alive at the conclusion of Ramadan, not merely at the time of the moon sighting. This establishes the principle that the obligation is tied to the state of existence during the final night of the month, distinguishing it from other forms of charity.
